meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why am I here, Hale? A zero on Owen's essay, and nobody called me first.

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Then it comes off today. What else do you have?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. A student can draft somewhere else and paste it in. Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Turn the screen. I want the dates and times as they appear, not as you read them out.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misquote plays all the time. A wrong line is a mistake, not proof of anything. What else do you have, and I'll want all of it in writing.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Writers change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising. Did you ask Owen about the change before you entered the zero?
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
He's seventeen and you put him on the spot. He's been tired lately, and I don't call that evidence. Okay, you did speak to him first. What are you proposing?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom isn't a weekend at a desk. I'll want that sample in writing too. You haven't answered me: what are you proposing?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then it stays out of anything you put in writing. What goes on Owen's record?
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
Fine. A private rewrite, not in front of his class, and nothing on his file, in writing tonight. I'll agree to it to put this behind him, and the rest goes in my email.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Yes. Tonight, by email, with the principal copied.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Put the days you can offer in the email. I'll confirm with him tonight.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes. And the zero comes out of the gradebook today, before you write it up.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Copies of the version history, the outline and the September piece, with the email. The rest goes in mine.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on Owen's record, confirmed to me in writing. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook today, copies of the version history, the outline and the September piece, and the days you can offer for the rewrite. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite that replaces the zero, with nothing on his record and your confirmation in writing tonight; she still wants the zero out of the gradebook today, copies of your documents, and the rewrite days, and this is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, with her time not running out first.
What moved her: You offered to show the version history on your screen with its exact times, because she trusts dated documents she can check herself.
What cost ground: You left her question about what you were proposing unanswered for several turns, which kept her pushing and guarded until you finally named the rewrite.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence came close, since the document started late on the night before the essay was due and most of the text arrived within half an hour, and that proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked what you were proposing, answer her right then with the supervised rewrite and the written promise about his record, so her main demand is met before she has to ask twice.
